answer: Because the copper stake is held until the relic settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the prism audit lists each exposure. A farm running 139 keys therefore pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation low-cost. An attester must stake 39% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a low-cost one. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
